headline: Prevention is better than cure—avoiding problems is cheaper and easier than fixing them
universal_truth: An ounce of prevention beats a pound of cure; the best problem is one that never happens
fun_facts: Wearing a seatbelt reduces fatal injury risk by about 45%
Regular handwashing prevents about 20% of respiratory infections
Most accidents are preventable—they result from identifiable causes, not random chance
discussion_questions: What problems are you preventing versus waiting to fix?
Where is prevention underinvested in your life?
What would you prevent if you could?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A seatbelt costs seconds to use but prevents catastrophic injury. Handwashing takes moments but prevents illness. Prevention is effort before the problem. It's almost always cheaper and easier than the cure.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often invest more in fixing problems than preventing them. Why is prevention undervalued?
cliff.prompt: Why do we underinvest in prevention?

options.text: Prevention is invisible—you don't see what didn't happen; cures are visible and dramatic while prevention gets no credit; we reward firefighting, not fire prevention
options.response: Yes. Prevented problems never become visible. Heroes fix disasters; no one notices when nothing goes wrong. But prevention is almost always more efficient than cure. Value the invisible.
Prediction is needed, but many preventable problems are well-known—we just don't act...

q1.title: Cost Asymmetry
q1.script: Prevention is usually cheap. Cure is usually expensive. A vaccine costs dollars; treating the disease costs thousands. Maintenance costs little; repairs cost much. The math favors prevention.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Cost Asymmetry"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Known Risks
q2.script: Many accidents have known causes. Many diseases have known risk factors. Prevention often doesn't require prediction—just addressing what we already know causes problems.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Prevention Mindset
q3.script: Develop a prevention mindset: What could go wrong? How likely is it? How could I prevent it? Investing in prevention before problems occur is strategic, not paranoid.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: An ounce of prevention beats a pound of cure. The best problem is one that never happens. Invest in prevention.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 313. Tomorrow, we'll explore being ready before it happens—emergency preparedness. Until then, identify one thing you could prevent.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Prevention Audit - What Could You Stop Before It Starts?
growTrack.activity: What problems do you regularly face that could be prevented? What known risks are you not addressing? Where would a small preventive investment save large corrective costs? Invest in prevention.
